easy.question: What are the Israelites forbidden to make according to verse 1?
answers: Idols
Sabbaths
Statutes

easy.question: What does the Torah command the Israelites to keep according to verse 2?
answers: The sanctuary
The Sabbaths
The idols
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Ye shall keep my sabbaths.”

easy.question: Who says, “Keep my commandments”?
answers: Moses
The people
The Lord
easy.explanation: The speaker is the Lord, as shown by the words “I am the Lord.”

medium.question: What is required of a person in verse 3?
answers: To walk in God’s statutes, keep His commandments, and do them
To build images and keep the Sabbath
To bow to stones and visit the sanctuary
medium.explanation: The verse connects following God’s statutes, keeping His commandments, and putting them into practice.

medium.question: What does the phrase “any image of stone ... to bow down unto it” refer to?

A stone set up for idolatrous worship
A stone used to mark a road

Verse 2 cancels the prohibitions in verse 1

To describe the appearance of the sanctuary
To show that the verses were spoken on the Sabbath
challenge.explanation: The phrase reinforces the Lord as the source and authority of these commands.

challenge.question: What do the actions “walk,” “keep,” and “do” in verse 3 suggest?

The commands must become practical behavior
The commandments concern only walking from place to place

challenge.question: What exactly is forbidden concerning the stone in verse 1?

Using a stone to build the sanctuary
Setting up a stone image in the land for people to bow down to

To show that the verses were spoken on the Sabbath

paragraphs.title: Blessed Rain and the Land’s Produce

easy.question: What does the Lord promise to give at the proper time?
answers: Rain
Wars
Taxes
easy.explanation: The verse says, “I will give you rain in due season.”

easy.question: What will the land produce?
answers: Water
Its increase
Stones
easy.explanation: The verse says, “the land shall yield her increase.”

easy.question: Where will the Israelites dwell safely?
answers: In the wilderness
In Egypt
In their land
easy.explanation: The verse promises that they will dwell safely in their land.

medium.question: What is the connection between rain in due season and the harvest?
answers: Timely rain helps the land produce crops
Rain prevents the land from producing
Rain causes people to leave the land
medium.explanation: The verse connects rain at the proper time with the land’s produce and the trees’ fruit.

medium.question: What sequence of events is described?
answers: Safety, then rain, and finally sowing
Rain and produce, followed by food and safety
Sowing, then famine, and finally exile
medium.explanation: Rain and crops come first; afterward the people eat their fill and dwell safely in the land.

medium.question: What does “threshing” mean in “your threshing shall reach unto the vintage”?
answers: Gathering grapes
Sowing a field
Separating grain from its stalks
medium.explanation: Threshing separates grain from the stalks. The context describes such an abundant harvest that threshing continues until the grape harvest.

challenge.question: What does “your threshing shall reach unto the vintage” show about the harvest?
answers: The harvest will continue with little gap between seasons
The grape harvest will fail every year
Threshing will occur only after years of famine
challenge.explanation: Threshing continuing until the vintage expresses abundance and a steady succession of crops.

challenge.question: Why is it important that rain comes “in due season,” not merely in large amounts?
answers: Rain always destroys crops
Agriculture depends on rain falling at the right time
Rain falls only during the vintage
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes the proper timing needed for crops to grow and ripen.

challenge.question: Which phrase shows that the blessing includes security as well as agricultural abundance?
answers: “The trees of the field shall yield their fruit”
“Ye shall eat your bread to the full”
“Ye shall dwell in your land safely”
challenge.explanation: Dwelling safely adds stability and security to the blessing of plentiful crops.

questions.question: What does “your threshing shall reach unto the vintage” show about the harvest?
answers: The harvest will continue with little gap between seasons
The grape harvest will fail every year
Threshing will occur only after years of famine
questions.explanation: Threshing continuing until the vintage expresses abundance and a steady succession of crops.

answers: Rain always destroys crops
Agriculture depends on rain falling at the right time
Rain falls only during the vintage
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes the proper timing needed for crops to grow and ripen.

questions.question: Which phrase shows that the blessing includes security as well as agricultural abundance?
answers: “The trees of the field shall yield their fruit”
“Ye shall eat your bread to the full”
“Ye shall dwell in your land safely”
questions.explanation: Dwelling safely adds stability and security to the blessing of plentiful crops.

easy.question: What will be given in the land?
answers: Peace
Rain
Wealth
easy.explanation: The verse says, “I will give peace in the land.”

easy.question: What will happen to the enemies?
answers: They will flee to the sea
They will fall before Israel by the sword
They will ask for peace
easy.explanation: The verse says they will fall before Israel by the sword.

easy.question: How many will chase ten thousand according to verse 8?
answers: Five
One thousand
One hundred
easy.explanation: The verse says that one hundred will put ten thousand to flight.

medium.question: What condition results from peace in the land?
answers: People can lie down without fear
The people must go to war
Enemies rule the land
medium.explanation: Peace means they can lie down without anyone making them afraid.

medium.question: What does the phrase “none shall make you afraid” describe?
answers: Someone bringing food
Freedom from anyone causing fear
Someone building a road
medium.explanation: The phrase describes sleeping peacefully without fear or alarm.

medium.question: What sequence is described in these verses?
answers: Enemies pursue Israel, then peace comes
Peace and security come first, followed by victory over enemies
Wild beasts attack, then Israel flees
medium.explanation: The passage first describes peace and safety, then Israel’s victory over its enemies.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from five chasing one hundred and one hundred chasing ten thousand?
answers: The same ratio applies in every situation
The victory is portrayed as far greater than ordinary human strength
Only five people are allowed to fight
challenge.explanation: The changing ratios highlight the extraordinary power of the victory.

challenge.question: Which detail in verse 6 shows safety from both wild animals and war?
answers: “I will rid evil beasts” and “neither shall the sword go through your land”
“I will give peace” and “ye shall chase your enemies”
“Ye shall lie down” and “they shall fall before you”
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly removes both the danger of wild beasts and the danger of war.

challenge.question: What does “neither shall the sword go through your land” mean?
answers: The Israelites may not leave their land
War will not pass through the land
Animals will not cross the roads
challenge.explanation: The sword represents warfare, so the phrase means that war will not pass through the land.

questions.question: What can be inferred from five chasing one hundred and one hundred chasing ten thousand?
answers: The same ratio applies in every situation
The victory is portrayed as far greater than ordinary human strength
Only five people are allowed to fight
questions.explanation: The changing ratios highlight the extraordinary power of the victory.

questions.question: Which detail in verse 6 shows safety from both wild animals and war?
answers: “I will rid evil beasts” and “neither shall the sword go through your land”
“I will give peace” and “ye shall chase your enemies”
“Ye shall lie down” and “they shall fall before you”
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly removes both the danger of wild beasts and the danger of war.

answers: The Israelites may not leave their land
War will not pass through the land
Animals will not cross the roads
questions.explanation: The sword represents warfare, so the phrase means that war will not pass through the land.

easy.question: What does the Lord promise Israel in verse 9?
answers: That they will be fruitful and multiply
That they will leave the land
That they will become slaves
easy.explanation: The Lord promises to make Israel fruitful and multiply them.

easy.question: What does the Lord promise to place among the Israelites?
answers: A palace
His tabernacle
A military camp
easy.explanation: The verse says, “I set my tabernacle among you.”

easy.question: From where did the Lord bring the Israelites?
answers: Canaan
The wilderness of Sinai
Egypt and slavery
easy.explanation: The Lord reminds Israel that He brought them out of Egypt so they would not be slaves.

medium.question: What will happen to the old grain when new grain appears?
answers: The old will be brought out to make room for the new
The new grain will be burned
Neither will be eaten
medium.explanation: The harvest will be so abundant that the old grain will be removed because of the new.

medium.question: What does “my soul shall not abhor you” mean?
answers: The Lord will forget Israel
The Lord will not reject or despise Israel
The Lord will bless idols
medium.explanation: The statement promises that the Lord will not reject or despise His people.

medium.question: What relationship between the Lord and Israel is described in verses 12–13?
answers: The Lord is only a foreign king
Israel will remain far from the Lord
The Lord will be Israel’s God, and Israel will be His people
medium.explanation: The passage describes a mutual covenant relationship between God and His people.

challenge.question: What does “the bands of your yoke” symbolize?
answers: The burden and slavery of servants
Musical instruments in the sanctuary
Boundary markers in the land
challenge.explanation: The bands of a yoke symbolize the bondage that the Lord broke.

challenge.question: What does “made you go upright” suggest?
answers: Walking bent over in fear
Walking upright with dignity and freedom
Sitting in the wilderness for a long time
challenge.explanation: After slavery is broken, Israel walks upright, symbolizing dignity and freedom.

challenge.question: What does the order of the promises in verses 9–13 show?
answers: The Lord promises only food
The Lord focuses only on the Exodus
The blessing includes abundance, divine presence, and a covenant relationship
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from fruitfulness and abundance to God’s presence, relationship, and freedom from slavery.

questions.question: What does “the bands of your yoke” symbolize?
answers: The burden and slavery of servants
Musical instruments in the sanctuary
Boundary markers in the land
questions.explanation: The bands of a yoke symbolize the bondage that the Lord broke.

questions.question: What does “made you go upright” suggest?
answers: Walking bent over in fear

Sitting in the wilderness for a long time
questions.explanation: After slavery is broken, Israel walks upright, symbolizing dignity and freedom.

answers: The Lord promises only food
The Lord focuses only on the Exodus
The blessing includes abundance, divine presence, and a covenant relationship
questions.explanation: The passage moves from fruitfulness and abundance to God’s presence, relationship, and freedom from slavery.

paragraphs.title: Breaking the Covenant and the First Punishments

easy.question: What will happen to the seed Israel sows?
answers: Their enemies will eat it
Their enemies will store it
It will be returned
easy.explanation: The verse says that Israel will sow seed in vain because enemies will eat it.

easy.question: What will happen if Israel does not listen or obey the commandments?
answers: They will receive great abundance
Punishments and troubles will come upon them
Their enemies will help them
easy.explanation: The passage describes disease, failed crops, and defeat for disobedience.

easy.question: What will Israel do because of its enemies?
answers: Defeat them
Make a covenant with them
Flee even when no one is pursuing
easy.explanation: The verse says they will flee when no one pursues them.

medium.question: Why will the seed be sown “in vain”?
answers: Because enemies will eat the crop
Because no one will sow it
Because it will be stored in barns
medium.explanation: The sowing will not benefit Israel because enemies will consume the harvest.

medium.question: What does “break my covenant” mean in this passage?
answers: To keep the covenant
To violate or abandon the covenant
To renew the covenant
medium.explanation: The context describes refusing the commandments and thereby violating the covenant.

medium.question: What sequence is described?
answers: Victory over enemies, followed by obedience
Rain and blessing, followed by disease
Disobedience, punishment, and defeat before enemies
medium.explanation: The people first reject the commandments and covenant; punishment and defeat follow.

challenge.question: What does “I also will do this unto you” emphasize?
answers: The Lord’s corresponding response to their actions
The cancellation of all punishments
A promise of victory in war
challenge.explanation: The Lord declares that He will respond to their rejection of His laws and covenant.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “ye shall flee when none pursueth you”?
answers: They will flee in order to attack a particular enemy
Fear will be so great that they flee without an immediate threat
They will remain calm during war
challenge.explanation: The absence of a pursuer shows that their flight comes from intense fear and panic.

challenge.question: What do “consume the eyes” and “cause sorrow of heart” describe?
answers: Joy after success
The produce of the land
Diseases and suffering affecting body and spirit
challenge.explanation: The phrases occur alongside consumption and burning fever and describe severe affliction.

questions.question: What does “I also will do this unto you” emphasize?
answers: The Lord’s corresponding response to their actions
The cancellation of all punishments
A promise of victory in war
questions.explanation: The Lord declares that He will respond to their rejection of His laws and covenant.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “ye shall flee when none pursueth you”?
answers: They will flee in order to attack a particular enemy

They will remain calm during war
questions.explanation: The absence of a pursuer shows that their flight comes from intense fear and panic.

questions.question: What do “consume the eyes” and “cause sorrow of heart” describe?
answers: Joy after success
The produce of the land
Diseases and suffering affecting body and spirit
questions.explanation: The phrases occur alongside consumption and burning fever and describe severe affliction.

He will cancel the punishment
He will give gifts

Iron
Wood
easy.explanation: The verse says, “I will make your heaven as iron.”

Branches
Fruit

medium.question: What will be the result of hard work in the land?

The harvest will greatly increase
The work will become easier
medium.explanation: The verse says their strength will be spent in vain.

medium.question: What sequence is described?

Pride is broken, the heavens and earth become hard, and finally there is no harvest
The trees produce fruit, then punishment begins
medium.explanation: The passage moves from broken pride to unyielding heavens and earth and finally to failed crops.

medium.question: What does “the pride of your power” refer to?
answers: The height of the mountains
Physical strength
Pride or confidence in one’s power
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to Israel’s pride and sense of security, which the Lord will break.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “your heaven as iron” and “your earth as brass”?
answers: There will be no rain, and the ground will not produce properly
The heavens and earth will protect the people
The land will be rich in metals
challenge.explanation: Iron heavens suggest no rain, while brass-like earth suggests soil that does not yield crops.

challenge.question: How does “your strength shall be spent in vain” relate to the end of the passage?
answers: The people will leave for another land
Their labor will be useless because the land and trees produce nothing
Their strength will grow because the harvest is abundant
challenge.explanation: Their effort will have no result because the land and trees will not yield produce.

challenge.question: What does “I will punish you seven times more” emphasize?

Punishment happens only once
The punishment will increase after earlier punishments have failed
challenge.explanation: “Seven times more” indicates intensified punishment after the people continue refusing to listen.

Their strength will grow because the harvest is abundant
questions.explanation: Their effort will have no result because the land and trees will not yield produce.

answers: Punishment will end immediately
Punishment happens only once
The punishment will increase after earlier punishments have failed
questions.explanation: “Seven times more” indicates intensified punishment after the people continue refusing to listen.

answers: Another plague will be added
They will receive a reward
They will receive peace
easy.explanation: The Lord says He will bring seven times more plagues if they continue refusing to listen.

easy.question: What will be sent among the people?
answers: Enemies from another land
Wild beasts
Angels
easy.explanation: The Lord says, “I will also send wild beasts among you.”

easy.question: What will the wild beasts do to the livestock?
answers: Protect them
Pasture them
Destroy them
easy.explanation: The wild beasts will destroy the cattle.

medium.question: What sequence is described?
answers: The people listen, and then blessing comes
The people remain defiant, and wild beasts are sent
The people repent, and then a plague comes
medium.explanation: The people refuse to listen, after which the Lord sends wild beasts among them.

medium.question: What does “your high ways shall be desolate” mean?
answers: The roads will be empty and abandoned
The roads will be wide and comfortable
The roads will be crowded
medium.explanation: Desolate roads are empty and abandoned because the population has been devastated.

medium.question: What does “will not be reformed by me” mean in this context?
answers: The people will not learn from the punishments
The people will stop working
The people will defeat the wild beasts
medium.explanation: The phrase describes people who do not change or take warning from the punishments.

challenge.question: What does it mean that the Lord will “walk contrary” to the people?
answers: He will ignore their actions completely
He will bless them regardless
He will respond to their opposition with corresponding judgment
challenge.explanation: Because the people oppose the Lord, He says He will act against them in response.

challenge.question: What does the repeated number seven emphasize?
answers: The punishment is severe and intensified
The punishment lasts only seven hours
The punishment occurs only once
challenge.explanation: The repetition of seven emphasizes the growing severity of the punishment.

challenge.question: What is the main difference between verses 21 and 24?
answers: Verse 21 describes blessing, while verse 24 describes a curse
Verse 21 begins the plagues, while verse 24 describes the Lord striking again after continued resistance
Verse 21 punishes Israel for others’ sins, while verse 24 does not punish them
challenge.explanation: Verse 21 begins the intensified punishments; verse 24 adds further judgment after continued opposition.

questions.question: What does it mean that the Lord will “walk contrary” to the people?

He will bless them regardless
He will respond to their opposition with corresponding judgment
questions.explanation: Because the people oppose the Lord, He says He will act against them in response.

The punishment occurs only once
questions.explanation: The repetition of seven emphasizes the growing severity of the punishment.

answers: Verse 21 describes blessing, while verse 24 describes a curse
Verse 21 begins the plagues, while verse 24 describes the Lord striking again after continued resistance
Verse 21 punishes Israel for others’ sins, while verse 24 does not punish them
questions.explanation: Verse 21 begins the intensified punishments; verse 24 adds further judgment after continued opposition.

easy.question: What will the Lord bring upon the people?
answers: A sword
Rain
Peace
easy.explanation: The verse says, “I will bring a sword upon you.”

easy.question: Where will the people gather?
answers: In the fields
In their cities
In the wilderness
easy.explanation: The verse says they will gather within their cities.

easy.question: What will happen when they eat?
answers: They will be completely satisfied
They will not eat at all
They will eat but not be satisfied
easy.explanation: The verse ends by saying, “ye shall eat, and not be satisfied.”

medium.question: What sequence is described?
answers: Sword, pestilence, being delivered to enemies, and then lack of bread
Abundant bread, peace, and victory over enemies
Rain, harvest, and celebration
medium.explanation: The passage describes sword, pestilence, enemy control, and then severe food shortage.

medium.question: What does “break the staff of your bread” mean?
answers: To give you more bread
To break the source of your food supply
To gather bread for the sanctuary
medium.explanation: A staff is a support; breaking the staff of bread means removing the support and supply of food.

medium.question: Why do ten women bake their bread in one oven?
answers: Because ovens and food are scarce
Because it is a festival custom
Because each woman brings a great deal of bread
medium.explanation: One oven for ten women and bread distributed by weight show severe shortage and rationing.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the bread being delivered “by weight”?
answers: Bread is distributed without limits
Bread is reserved only for enemies
Bread is distributed in measured portions because of scarcity
challenge.explanation: Weighing the bread shows that each person receives a limited, exact amount.

challenge.question: How is breaking the “staff of bread” connected with “ye shall eat, and not be satisfied”?
answers: When the food supply is broken, eating still does not bring satisfaction
When there is more bread, people eat less
The two statements are unrelated
challenge.explanation: The broken food supply leaves too little bread for people to become full.

challenge.question: Which detail especially emphasizes the severity of the situation?
answers: The sword is mentioned before the cities
Ten women use one oven and the bread is weighed
The people gather in their cities
challenge.explanation: The shared oven and weighed bread vividly portray extreme scarcity.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the bread being delivered “by weight”?
answers: Bread is distributed without limits
Bread is reserved only for enemies
Bread is distributed in measured portions because of scarcity
questions.explanation: Weighing the bread shows that each person receives a limited, exact amount.

answers: When the food supply is broken, eating still does not bring satisfaction

The two statements are unrelated

answers: The sword is mentioned before the cities

The people gather in their cities
questions.explanation: The shared oven and weighed bread vividly portray extreme scarcity.

easy.question: What do the people refuse to do?
answers: Listen to the Lord
Eat
Go to war
easy.explanation: The verse says, “ye will not ... hearken unto me.”

easy.question: How do the people act toward the Lord?
answers: With love
In opposition
With joy
easy.explanation: The passage says they walk contrary to the Lord.

easy.question: What does the Lord say He will do?
answers: Give them gifts
Send them to rest
Chastise them
easy.explanation: The Lord says He will chastise them seven times for their sins.

medium.question: Why will the Lord act against the people in fury?
answers: They refuse to listen and continue opposing Him
They immediately ask forgiveness
They keep all the commandments
medium.explanation: Their continued refusal to listen and opposition bring further judgment.

medium.question: What does “walk contrary unto me” mean in this context?
answers: To move quickly
To oppose the Lord and disregard His warnings
To act humbly
medium.explanation: The phrase describes treating the Lord’s commands as something to resist or ignore.

medium.question: What sequence is described?
answers: The Lord chastises them, then they begin sinning
The people refuse to listen and oppose the Lord, then He chastises them
The people repent, then the Lord punishes them
medium.explanation: The people’s refusal and opposition come first; the Lord’s chastisement follows.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the movement from “ye walk contrary unto me” to “I also will walk contrary unto you”?

Only the people act in the chapter
The Lord does not respond to the people
challenge.explanation: The wording presents the people’s actions followed by the Lord’s corresponding response.

challenge.question: What does “I also” emphasize?
answers: The Lord agrees to forgive immediately
The Lord will respond with severity as well
The Lord does not know what the people did
challenge.explanation: “I also” stresses that the Lord will act in response to the people’s conduct.

challenge.question: What can be understood from “seven times for your sins”?
answers: The suffering will be minor
The punishment will occur only once
The punishment will be severe and increased because of their sins
challenge.explanation: Seven conveys intensity and abundance, indicating severe punishment for their sins.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the movement from “ye walk contrary unto me” to “I also will walk contrary unto you”?
answers: The people and the Lord are portrayed as acting in response to each other
Only the people act in the chapter
The Lord does not respond to the people
questions.explanation: The wording presents the people’s actions followed by the Lord’s corresponding response.

questions.question: What does “I also” emphasize?
answers: The Lord agrees to forgive immediately
The Lord will respond with severity as well
The Lord does not know what the people did
questions.explanation: “I also” stresses that the Lord will act in response to the people’s conduct.

questions.question: What can be understood from “seven times for your sins”?
answers: The suffering will be minor
The punishment will occur only once
The punishment will be severe and increased because of their sins
questions.explanation: Seven conveys intensity and abundance, indicating severe punishment for their sins.

paragraphs.title: Social Collapse and the Destruction of High Places

easy.question: Whose flesh will the Israelites eat?
answers: The flesh of their sons and daughters
The flesh of the priests
The flesh of their enemies
easy.explanation: The passage explicitly says they will eat the flesh of their sons and daughters.

easy.question: What will the Lord destroy?
answers: Israel’s cities
Israel’s high places
Israel’s fields
easy.explanation: The verse says, “I will destroy your high places.”

easy.question: Which two groups of children are mentioned?
answers: Infants and children
Sons and firstborns
Sons and daughters
easy.explanation: The verse specifically mentions sons and daughters.

medium.question: What sequence is described?

First the high places are built, and then children are eaten
First there is peace, and then cities are built
medium.explanation: Verse 29 describes the eating of sons and daughters; verse 30 describes destruction of high places and idols.

medium.question: What are the “images” and “idols” in this context?

Objects used in idolatrous worship
Priestly garments
medium.explanation: Their association with high places and idols shows that they are objects of false worship.

medium.question: How are destroying the high places and casting corpses on idols related?
answers: Both describe a religious celebration
Both describe building the sanctuary
Both express punishment and contempt for idolatry
medium.explanation: The destruction and desecration of idols show judgment against false worship.

challenge.question: What does “my soul shall abhor you” express?
